subject: Re: Nimbus - Performance SLO & Concurrency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus discovery — perf/SLO recap and next steps

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the performance and SLO items we discussed so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps: 

- Latency target: 95th pctile <= 250ms for single-request generation (avg seq len ~120 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 10 requests/sec with bursts to 30 rps for short windows (no more than 5 minutes).
- Concurrency: pool of ~25-30 parallel active requests across your service instances. You noted spikes up to ~60 concurrent connections during peak campaigns.
- Streaming: need server-sent events for partial token streaming to the browser (client cancels mid-stream ~10% of requests).
- Connection pooling: prefer persistent HTTP/2 connections from the app layer; will open ~120 simultaneous sockets across 4 app nodes.
- Quota expectations: initial pilot request for a higher concurrency quota (50 concurrent requests) and higher burst quota for 2 weeks to validate load.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura and I to propose a pilot quota and rate-limit config for your account by EOD tomorrow.
2) Your ops team to share a short traffic sample (per-endpoint qps, connection counts) — a spreadsheet is fine.
3) If pilot looks good, we’ll map to a Dedicated capacity recommendation and formalize in the proposal.

Attachment: nimtech_slo_requirements.pdf (your annotated SLO doc)

Looping Laura for the quota proposal. Logan I'm copying you for capacity sizing guidance if we need a temporary burst pool.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches what we have internally. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The 60 concurrent figure is across all pods; per-node concurrency is closer to 20 but we do see short spikes where a single pod handles ~35.
- Streaming is used for progressive rendering in the web app; cancel rates spike to ~25% on search-heavy pages.
- We can deliver a 7-day traffic sample; attaching the primary sheet.

Attachment: nimbus_prod_traffic.xlsx

On the pilot quota: we’d like to test with 50 concurrent and a burst allowance up to 100 rps for 10 minutes. If you can provision that for a two-week pilot we’ll validate user-facing metrics and return an SLO decision.

One ask on rate limits: can Redwood provide per-route quotas (search vs chat) rather than a single global pool? We have very different traffic shapes between the two.

—Jane

Thanks Jane — helpful detail. Laura and I discussed and here's what we can do for the pilot and how we'd handle per-route quotas: 

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
- Concurrency quota: 50 concurrent connections reserved for NimTech across your cluster.
- Burst quota: allow up to 100 requests/sec for 10-minute rolling windows, with a smooth-down policy to avoid thundering.
- Per-route logical quotas: we can partition the concurrency pool into logical buckets (e.g., search=35, chat=15) and enforce route-level soft limits with weighted fairness. Hard global cap remains to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Streaming: enable SSE streaming endpoints; we will not count idle connections towards active concurrency once the request has completed server-side token emission (reduces your effective concurrency load).

Operational notes:
- We will instrument token-level latency tracking for the pilot and provide daily summaries (p95/p99).
- If you need more per-node headroom, we can enable short-lived burstCapacity that routes to a Dedicated burst pool (additional cost applies).

Logan — can you confirm whether we have headroom in our pilot pool next week to allocate 50 reserved conc + 100 rps burst for NimTech? Also flag if we need AM approval for temporary burst capacity.

If this sounds good Jane I'll put together a short two-week pilot addendum (DocuSign link) and a proposed pricing estimate.

Thanks,
Marissa
